title: No Names Below
summary: The Mirage Club is a refuge built around a strict social rule: nobody asks for a real name below street level. Isabelle breaks that rule the moment she sees Kael and calls him Merrit.

panelPlan.text: Wide interior: subterranean club during a quiet performance interval, crowded but intimate. A hand-painted sign by the stairs reads NO NAMES BELOW.
Kael, Eva and Jessa enter looking for shade and a meal. Isabelle stops mid-conversation across the room when she sees Kael.
She crosses the floor and says Merrit. The room goes noticeably quiet because she has violated the club's rule, not because anyone else recognizes him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: Merrit.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I am sorry, ma'am. You have the wrong man.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: Do not do that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: He is not doing anything. That is the trouble.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Merrit. That is a new one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: You brought witnesses?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I brought two people who would not stay behind.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That is not what happened.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: It is close enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Can we eat before this gets worse?

directionInline.text: The community's social norm, not a technical setting, drives the scene. Isabelle's recognition is intimate and disruptive because names are deliberately suspended here.

title: The Room Takes Sides
summary: Isabelle accuses Kael of abandoning the club during an old crackdown. Because she has broken the no-names rule, the club splits over whether her grievance deserves an exception. Kael becomes the center of a conflict he does not own.

panelPlan.text: Isabelle and Kael face each other at a copper table. Patrons deliberately turn chairs away while still listening.
A longtime patron tells Isabelle to drop it; another says Merrit owes the room an answer. Eva watches the social fault line spread.
Kael sets his untouched drink aside and asks Isabelle one concrete question: what does she actually want from the man she thinks he is?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: You left us with the doors chained.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I was not here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: You always could make anything sound reasonable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: What if he is telling the truth?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: He is not.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: What do you want from Merrit?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: I want him to admit he left us here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Then I am afraid I cannot give you that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: You could apologize.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I cannot apologize for him. I can listen if that is what you need.

directionInline.text: Avoid clipped call-and-response cadence. Isabelle should have emotional specificity; Kael's question redirects from identity debate to the human need underneath it.

title: The Man Who Promised
summary: Eva learns that Isabelle was not merely surprised by Kael: a traveling preacher recently told her that Merrit would return before the next flare. Jessa recognizes that this is no longer just rumor chasing them.

panelPlan.text: In a side corridor, Eva follows Isabelle while Jessa waits by the stairs. Isabelle retrieves an old photograph with a man's face partly burned away; the resemblance to Kael is suggestive but not conclusive.
Isabelle says the preacher knew details about Merrit he should not have known. Eva's excitement finally gives way to unease.
Jessa takes the photograph, compares it to Kael across the room, and hands it back without declaring a match.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Who told you he was coming?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: A preacher with dust in every seam of his coat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Did he give you a name?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: Samuel. Maybe.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: What did he want?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: Nothing. That is what bothered me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Nobody walks that far for nothing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: He wanted me here when Merrit came.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: So somebody is putting Kael in front of people on purpose.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Maybe.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Maybe?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: A preacher told one woman a story. That is what preachers do.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You do not believe that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I believe I want more than one answer before I scare myself.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You get scared?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Constantly. I just do not make it a hobby.

directionInline.text: This is the first clearly prepared encounter, but still no proof that Samuel knows Kael or coordinates with anyone.

title: What He Left
summary: Isabelle brings Kael to the locked room Merrit abandoned years earlier. Instead of arguing about resemblance, Kael helps her face what was actually left behind: ordinary possessions and no grand explanation.

panelPlan.text: Isabelle unlocks a cramped storage room preserved more by avoidance than reverence. Kael stays at the threshold until she enters first.
They find a coat, a broken instrument case, letters never sent. Eva hangs back, understanding that curiosity has limits.
Isabelle holds one letter but cannot open it. Kael takes no object and makes no claim on Merrit's life.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: He said he would come back for these.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Maybe he meant to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: That is generous.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: No. It is only possible.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: You do not want to know what is in the letter?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: No, ma'am. It is not mine.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: We can give you some privacy.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: You can stay.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Are you sure?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: You have been trying to know everything since you walked in. You may as well learn what it costs.

directionInline.text: Keep the scene emotionally grounded. The mystery creates access to unresolved human material, but Kael does not become a vessel for the absent man.

title: One Lie Too Many
summary: Eva proposes a test: tell the club Kael is someone entirely different and see whether the story changes. Kael refuses to turn Isabelle's grief into an experiment, establishing a boundary that will matter when Veyra's methods are revealed.

panelPlan.text: Eva catches Kael and Jessa near the stairs and quietly proposes giving the room a false name to see who repeats it.
Kael stops walking. His objection is not about being studied; it is about using Isabelle and the room as instruments.
Isabelle overhears enough to understand. Instead of being offended by Kael, she directs her anger at the unseen preacher who primed her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: What if we give them another name? Something obviously fake. If it spreads, we know somebody is carrying it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You have not even heard the name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I do not need to. Isabelle is not a test.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: She is trying to find out how the story travels.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I know what she is trying to do.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Then what is wrong with it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: They are people, Eva. They do not stop being people because you have a question.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: He is right.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You could both stop sounding so pleased about it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I am not pleased.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: Neither am I. The preacher already used me once.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: All right. No test.

directionInline.text: This page separates Eva's investigative appetite from Veyra's willingness to manipulate communities. Eva can cross lines, but Kael and consequences teach her where those lines are.

title: A Shadow on the Glass
summary: The trio leaves with a concrete lead, Samuel, but no explanation for why the planted story fit Isabelle's history so well. In the club's street-level glass, Kael's reflection briefly overlays the damaged photograph, an ordinary visual coincidence that lands harder because everyone is looking for meaning.

panelPlan.text: At the stairs, Isabelle returns the old photograph to its envelope rather than giving it to Eva. She and Kael part without resolution but without pretending he is Merrit.
Outside, Eva writes Samuel in her small ledger. Jessa asks where she intends to look for a preacher in the whole Sunfields.
Final panel: in dusty storefront glass, Kael's reflection lines up with the burned-away half of the photograph still visible through Isabelle's hand inside. It could be nothing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabelle
dialogueInline.text: If you see him, tell him I do not like being prepared.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: If he comes back here, tell him yourself.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Samuel Hayes. Maybe.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: A first name and a maybe. Excellent.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: It is more than we had yesterday.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Yesterday was quieter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: You hated yesterday.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I did not hate it. I respected it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Do you really think he does not care?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: No. I think he cares about people and not explanations.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That is worse.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: For you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: For him too. He just does not know it yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: You really need him to be a mystery, do you not?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You really need him not to be.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Maybe.

directionInline.text: End on ambiguous visual rhyme, not supernatural proof. The characters leave with a human lead.
